LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT

All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS

Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.

CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  January 12, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:21 p.m. on January
12, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine,
California; Mayor Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Larry Agran*
  Councilmember  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan
  *Via teleconference

Mayor Khan announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications
Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, the e-comment feature had been extended for all agenda items, which
allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments through the public
comment portion of each item and would be included as part of the official record and
uploaded to the City’s website. She also assured the community that the City of Irvine
was adhering to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout
City Hall by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.

Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.
 City Council Minutes  January 12, 2021

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Kuo led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Frank Winans from Woodbridge Community Church provided the invocation.

  1.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  1.1  Proclaim January 13, 2021, as “Korean American Day”

  Carl Petersen, Interim City Clerk, noted that one e-comment had been
  received from Sophia Stewart, Irvine resident, who noted her support for
  the “Korean American Day” proclamation.

  Mayor Khan announced that due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the City
  Council was unable to invite members from the community to attend the
  presentation in person; however, she was pleased to continue the annual
  recognition of the special day that celebrates the Korean American
  community, and presented a proclamation recognizing January 13, 2021,
  as “Korean American Day.” Vice Mayor Kim also expressed her
  appreciation to Korean American residents, its businesses, and nonprofit
  organizations.

  1.2  Proclaim January 18, 2021, as “Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Day”

  Carl Petersen, Interim City Clerk, noted that one e-comment had been
  received from Kevin Corrigan, who noted his support for the “Dr. Martin
  Luther King, Jr. Day” proclamation.

  Mayor Khan similarly noted that due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the City
  Council was unable to invite members from the community to attend the
  presentation in person; however, she was pleased to continue the annual
  recognition of the special day that honors the legacy of Dr. Martin Luther
  King, Jr., and presented a proclamation recognizing January 18, 2021,
  as “Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Day.”

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  January 12, 2021

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Agran presented a brief memo and presentation regarding the Build the
  Great Park veterans Cemetery Initiative (Initiative) that was adopted by the City Council
  last year, noting that he has prepared a resolution for consideration at the next City
  Council meeting that would implement provisions of the Initiative and the will of the
  people to designate the Amended and Stated Redevelopment Agreement (ARDA) site
  as the preferred location for the Veterans Cemetery. He also provided a brief history of
  the initiative and potential next steps to develop the cemetery.

  Mayor Khan asked City Attorney Melching to opine on the purpose of Council
  Announcements, to which City Attorney Melching clarified that Council Announcements
  was a time for the City Council to announce activities that members are engaged in, and
  as done previously, this section would be an appropriate time to ask for a future agenda
  item; however, he also noted that this section was not appropriate to lay out an argument
  for a position on a future agenda item.

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Agran to request the support of a second
  Councilmember to bring forward his proposed memo and resolution designating
  the ARDA site as the preferred site for the Veterans Cemetery, and pursuing
  further development at this site, for consideration at the January 26 City Council
  meeting.

  Mayor Khan noted that she would support the bringing this item forward after the
  feasibility study had been received from CalVet, to which Councilmember Agran
  expressed concern that the CalVet feasibility study would not be received until May, and
  that the purpose of the resolution was to commence construction by virtue of demolition,
  site clearance, and retention of historic features, within 30 to 60 days.

  Motion failed due to lack of second.

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  •  In response to the Coronavirus pandemic, two task forces have been established
  that will guide the City in 2021 and beyond. The COVID-19 and Business
  Reopening Task Forces are comprised of local health officials and business
  leaders who have a clear understanding of the issues faced during these
  extraordinary times and can offer insight on how to best overcome them. The
  COVID-19 Task Force will help navigate and advise the City Council on COVID-
  19 response efforts, helping to ensure the safety of the community is at the
  forefront of Council decisions. The task force is comprised of: 1) City Management
  staff and Mayor Khan; 2) Dr. Marnie Baker with MemorialCare; 3) Orange County
  Health Officer Dr. Clayton Chau; 4) Amy Durham, Director of Development for the
  National Alliance on Mental Illness; 5) Dr. Shruti Gohil from UC Irvine’s School of
  Medicine; 6) Dr. Grace Lozinski from Hoag; and 7) Dr. Hassan Movahedi from
  Kaiser Permanente. The Task Force will hold a Virtual Town Hall regarding
  COVID-19 vaccines on Friday, January 29 from 12 to 1:30 p.m. and the City will
  provide additional information about how to sign up in the coming days.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  January 12, 2021

  The Business Reopening Task Force will assist the City’s efforts to help promote
  small business growth, support local entrepreneurship, target industry relocation
  within City boundaries, and assist the City in remaining responsive to the business
  community. The Task Force will hold its first meeting on January 14 and includes
  the following members: 1) Jeff Davis, Vice President – Entitlement at Irvine
  Company; 2) Bryan Starr, President and CEO of the Greater Irvine Chamber of
  Commerce; 3) Dianne Markis, General Manager of the Marriot Irvine Spectrum; 4)
  Pamela Waitt, President of the OC Restaurant Association; and 5) Lucy Dunn,
  President and CEO of the Orange County Business Council.

  •  Last week, the City launched “Irvine Cares,” the first initiative of the COVID-19
  Task Force. Irvine Cares invites community members to slow the spread of
  COVID-19 by pledging support of mitigation measures, which include action as an
  advocate to ensure the health and safety of Irvine’s most vulnerable. Community
  members can take the pledge online or download a pledge card and mail it into the
  City. Once the pledge is signed, names will be included on the “I Pledge” website,
  and anyone who takes the pledge will receive an Irvine Cares face mask, sticker,
  and decal to highlight their commitment to being kind and protecting our
  community. The City invites you to share the pledge on social media using the
  hashtag IrvineCares (#IrvineCares). For more information and to take the pledge,
  visit cityofirvine.org/irvinecares.

  •  The City has created a new weekly e-newsletter as an additional way for the
  community to stay connected. The newsletter will be emailed to subscribers every
  Friday afternoon and will include information about ongoing projects, upcoming
  meetings and events, announcements, and items of note, such as how the City will
  celebrate its 50th anniversary this year. To read the first two editions and subscribe
  to the newsletter, visit cityofirvine.org.
